title: Staying Qualified: 35 Hours Every 5 Years
whatItIs: Your Driver CPC lasts 5 years. To keep it, do 35 hours of periodic training before the deadline on your card. There's no exam: you get a certificate of attendance.

keyFacts.text: You MUST do 35 hours of periodic training every 5 years to keep your Driver CPC.

keyFacts: It's illegal to drive professionally after your deadline without the training: fine up to £1,000.
International Driver CPC courses last at least 7 hours; National courses at least 3 hours 30 minutes.
Up to 12 of the 35 hours can be e-learning.
Training counts for 5 years from the date you took the course.
If you drive both lorries and buses, one set of 35 hours covers both.

visual.caption: Which Driver CPC training and card you need

items.title: International Driver CPC
items.text: Only International courses, 35 hours. You can drive professionally in the UK and Europe.

items.title: National Driver CPC
items.text: National courses or a mix. UK only: the card says 'Domestic UK use only'.

items.title: Return to Driving course
items.text: CPC expired less than 2 years ago? 7 hours, then 28 more hours within 12 months.

items.title: Driver CPC card (DQC)
items.text: Carry it while driving professionally. £50 fixed penalty if you drive without it.

a.label: International Driver CPC
points: Drive professionally in the UK and Europe
Only International courses (at least 7 hours each)

b.label: National Driver CPC
points: Drive professionally in the UK only
National courses (at least 3 hours 30 minutes) or a mix

onTheTest.question: How many hours of periodic training must you complete every 5 years to keep your Driver CPC?
onTheTest.why: You must do 35 hours of periodic training every 5 years to keep your Driver CPC to drive a lorry, bus or coach.

onTheTest.question: What is the most e-learning that can count towards your 35 hours of Driver CPC training?
onTheTest.why: You can only do up to 12 hours of e-learning (online courses with interactive videos or presentations) as part of your 35 hours.

traps: There's no test at the end of a course: you attend and get a certificate, which your employer can't keep.
Include any National course in your 35 hours and you get a National (UK only) card.
Training taken more than 5 years ago no longer counts towards the 35 hours.
You can't repeat the same course in a 5-year period without a good reason.
